summary: Iter 12 narrow retest of the 3 previously-failing tap-accumulation tools in ProMappingStudio. FIX VERIFIED: onPointerUp's new `else if (['triangle','corners','bullet'].includes(d.tool)) { /* no-op */ }` branch (ProMappingStudio.jsx line 235-237) correctly preserves the in-progress draft between taps. All 3 tools now auto-commit on the expected Nth tap. Triangle: 3rd tap goes 0->1 element. Corners: 4th tap goes 1->2 element. Bullet (with field-input text 'Driver Bullet'): 2nd tap goes 2->3 element. studio-inspector-list shows 'TRIANGLE triangle', 'CORNER BOX corner_box', 'BULLET Driver Bullet ARIAL / HELVETICA'. Secondary dashboard schema.version===2 clean SVG render case: seeded driver_profiles row so DriverProfileDialog did NOT auto-open; Template saved from Studio with schema.version=2 navigates to /dashboard with 'Template activated' toast. However the preview modal requires an active trip session, which requires a 3-step Start-New-Trip wizard (When? -> Load Type -> Template pick). Test got past step 1 (session-type-new) and into step 2 (Load Type: Store/Warehouse + Dairy/Water sub-question); wizard-next-2 stayed disabled because the test harness could not auto-select the correct Load Type combination for this driver. Without an active session the paper-sheet preview is not reachable, so the SVG-vs- assertion could not be executed. Code path looks correct per DynamicPaperSheet.jsx L22 (schema.version===2 -> ) but was not visually verified in this run.

critical_code_review_comments: ProMappingStudio.jsx onPointerUp (line 235-237) fix is correct and minimal. Consider making this branch assertive: `if (['triangle','corners','bullet'].includes(d.tool)) return;` at the top of onPointerUp so future drag-tool additions cannot accidentally reintroduce the regression.
ProMappingStudio.jsx still uses window.prompt() for grid rows/cols (line 205-206) — unreliable on mobile Safari and blocks automated UI tests. Replace with an inline popover.
ProMappingStudio.jsx is ~870 lines in one file, over the 700-line guideline. Extract CleanReconstructionCanvas, InspectorPane, AssetsPane into sibling files to shrink the main file under ~400 lines.

SessionWizard step 2 (Load Type) has a disabled Next that does NOT expose a single stable testid indicating which sub-option is selected. Add data-testid attributes to session-load-store/session-load-warehouse/session-load-dairy/session-load-water and expose wizard-load-ready state so automated tests can drive this flow.

DynamicPaperSheet renders the clean-render SVG only when the active trip session has a linked template whose schema.version===2 — recommend exposing a data-testid='paper-sheet-schema-version' attribute on the outer <div data-testid='paper-sheet'> to make the version branching directly observable from tests.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The 3 tap-accumulation tools (triangle/corners/bullet) are verified working. Canvas in Pro Studio is only ~184x184 px on desktop viewport — ALL tap coordinates MUST be computed as fractions of the canvas bounding_box (see the pt(fx, fy) helper in this iteration's script); earlier attempts that hardcoded px offsets like box.x+200 landed OUTSIDE the canvas and silently did nothing. For the dashboard schema.version===2 paper-sheet assertion, the blocker is SessionWizard step 2 (Load Type) — either (a) pre-insert a trip_sessions document directly in MongoDB with template_id pointing at the saved v2 template and reload /dashboard, or (b) have the main agent add stable testids (session-load-store, session-load-warehouse, session-load-dairy, session-load-water) to the SessionWizard step-2 option buttons so automation can drive it. DynamicPaperSheet.jsx L22 branching to CleanReconstructionCanvas for schema.version===2 is code-confirmed correct but not visually verified this run.
rca of the issue: Iter 11 bug RCA was precise: onPointerUp fell into the trailing `else { setDraft(null); }` for tap-accumulation tools and wiped draft.points between taps. Iter 12 confirms the fix: explicit `else if (['triangle','corners','bullet'].includes(d.tool)) { /* no-op */ }` branch preserves the accumulator so onPointerDown's auto-commit on the Nth tap (length===3 for triangle, length===4 for corners, second-tap for bullet) now fires as designed.
